steps: Confirm for me which hob this is — does the front burner produce a visible flame when the others are lit, and is this a gas hob with burners rather than a flat ceramic or induction surface?
Without touching anything on the hob, tell me what you see and hear at the front burner when you turn it on: does it click steadily, and does any flame appear at all, even briefly?
Look at the other burners while they're lit and tell me what colour the flame is — blue, or yellow/orange — and whether there's any sooting or black marks on your pans.
Look at the front burner (no touching, no lifting) and tell me whether the metal cap on top looks sat flat and level compared with the other burners, or whether it looks tilted or out of place.
Stop using the front burner for now and let me know what you've observed — I'll get a registered gas engineer booked, as a gas burner that won't light is engineer-only work.
output.diagnostic_question: When you turn the front burner on, does it click continuously with no flame at all, and are the other burners' flames blue rather than yellow or orange?
output.safety_note: This is a gas appliance, so by law only a registered gas engineer may work on it. Please do not lift, clean, dry or reseat any burner caps or parts, and do not keep trying to light the front burner. If you ever smell gas, see a yellow or orange flame, notice sooting on your pans, or smell burning, stop using the hob immediately and tell us or your onsite team straight away.

steps: First, can you tell me what kind of hob it is — does it have a glass surface you put pans straight onto, or does it have gas flames and metal pan supports? If you're not sure, a photo of the hob top would help.
If it's a glass-surfaced hob: check the control panel for a small key or padlock symbol lit up. That's a child lock and it can stop zones heating. Let me know if you can see one.
Check the wall switch above the worktop that powers the hob is switched on, and tell me whether your other kitchen appliances — kettle, microwave — are working normally.

If it's a glass hob with no flames, try this: hold a fridge magnet against the base of the pan you normally use. If it doesn't stick firmly, that pan won't heat on those rings. Try a pan the magnet grips and see whether those two rings then work.
output.diagnostic_question: Which type of hob is it — glass surface or gas flames — and with the child lock off and a magnet-sticking pan, do those two rings heat up now?
output.safety_note: If this is a gas hob, please don't attempt anything at all beyond looking and telling me what you see — don't lift, clean or reseat any burner caps, and don't keep trying to relight a burner. Gas work is restricted by law to registered engineers. If you smell gas, or see yellow or orange flames or sooty marks on your pans, stop using the hob and tell me straight away. Also please don't touch the fuse box or try to reset anything there, and don't move or pull out the hob.
